subject: Notice windows & auto-renew: TFC carveout proposal for ClearPath
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@clearpath.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpath.com
Date: 2027-04-25T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on T&C: notice windows and auto-renew

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for sending the MSA + order form. Our legal team did a pass and we have a couple of asks specifically around Term / Auto-Renew / Termination for Convenience (TFC):

- Auto-renew notice: the current order form requires a 90-day opt-out window. We generally push for 30 days in our vendor contracts. Can you confirm flexibility here?
- Notice window: we typically ask for a 30-day convenience termination notice for pilots / proof-of-concepts. The MSA has a 60-day minimum; is there any carveout for pilot SKUs?
- TFC language: we would prefer a limited TFC for pilot/non-production SKUs or an earlier notice paired with a scaled-offboarding credit rather than a blanket 60-day fee.

I've attached our redlines (ClearPath_Redlines_v3.pdf) with line-item comments. We're keen to move quickly on this (deal team is requesting execution by end of next week).

Can we get an internal alignment + a short legal sync this week? We can make time for a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Sara Klein
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClearPath Systems

Attachment: ClearPath_Redlines_v3.pdf (redlines PDF with inline comments)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@clearpath.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on T&C: notice windows and auto-renew

Sara — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. We're aligned on moving quickly. Proposed next steps:

1) Internal quick sync today (15–20m) to agree on negotiation posture. Ben / Karthik, can you join?
2) Legal proposal back to ClearPath with two options:
   - Option A (preferred by Redwood legal): Maintain 60-day notice, keep 90-day auto-renew opt-out; offer a one-time "pilot credit" (30% credit on first-month invoice) for pilot SKUs and a 60-day data export window at no charge.
   - Option B (commercial compromise): 30-day convenience notice limited to pilot SKUs only (defined by SKU list), 60-day for full production; auto-renew opt-out reduced to 60 days for pilot orders only.

We should surface what Laura / CS can operationally deliver for a 30-day pilot offboarding (playbook, data export SLA). Karthik, Ben — want your redline language and any non-starters.

I'll block 20m at 1:30pm PT and will include a short agenda.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: forwarding ClearPath_Redlines_v3.pdf to internal reviewers

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on T&C: notice windows and auto-renew

Quick legal stance and proposed text. TL;DR: full company-wide 30-day TFC is a non-starter. We can offer a scoped pilot carveout with operational guardrails.

Legal rationale:
- 60-day notice is standard to allow controlled offboarding and to preserve capacity planning for reserved/dedicated customers.
- Auto-renew reduction to 30 days increases churn risk and impacts capacity forecasting (esp. for Dedicated pools).

Suggested commercial/legal compromise (to put in the order form):

"Termination for Convenience (Pilot Orders). Notwithstanding Section X (Termination for Convenience), Customer may terminate Pilot Orders with thirty (30) days' prior written notice provided that (i) the terminated Pilot Orders are limited to SKUs listed in Schedule A (Pilot SKU Schedule), (ii) Customer shall provide Redwood reasonable cooperation for data export and transition, and (iii) no more than two (2) Pilot Orders may be terminated under this carveout in any 12-month period. For avoidance of doubt, Production Orders shall remain subject to the sixty (60) day notice set forth in Section X."

Auto-renew language suggestion (targeted):

"Auto-Renew (Pilot Orders): For Pilot Orders, the auto-renew notice period is sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. For Production Orders the auto-renew period remains ninety (90) days."

Operational concessions to offer ClearPath:
- 30% one-time pilot credit applied to the first post-activation invoice for Pilot Orders.
- 60-day complimentary data export and transitional assistance for terminated Pilot Orders.
- A small runbook (Schedule B) describing offboarding steps and responsibilities.

I've attached a marked-up Word with the two suggested clauses: Redwood_TFC_Proposal_20270425.docx. If sales wants to offer Option B (30-day opt-out for pilots with broader terms), we need to limit to specific SKUs and cap the number of pilot terminations.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_TFC_Proposal_20270425.docx (suggested clause text and redlines)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@clearpath.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on T&C: notice windows and auto-renew

Sara — appreciate the clarity and the timeline. From a Customer Success perspective, we can support the pilot carveout but need to document expectations up front. Proposed operational items to include in Schedule B: 

- Definition of Pilot SKU and how it's listed/changed (SKU list in order form)
- Offboarding checklist (data export contact, timeline, snapshot retention period)
- SLAs for data export: initial export within 10 business days, full handoff within 60 calendar days
- Limitations: pilot capacity is best-effort; no guaranteed dedicated capacity during pilot unless purchased.

If you can confirm which SKUs are considered "pilot" and the expected go-live/termination dates, we will draft the Schedule B and include the runbook language. Happy to join the legal call if helpful.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success (North America)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on T&C: notice windows and auto-renew

Hi all — thanks for the quick turnaround and the options. After reviewing Karthik's language with our GC, ClearPath can accept the pilot carveout language with a couple small edits:

- We agree to Pilot Orders being limited to a SKU schedule, but we want the cap to be three (3) Pilot Orders terminated in a 12-month period (rather than two).
- Auto-renew for Pilot Orders: 60 days is workable; we ask that the production auto-renew remain 90 days.
- Data export: we request a 90-day complimentary data export window (instead of 60) for terminated Pilot Orders (our internal teams run longer migrations).

If you can update the language accordingly, we can circulate the amended order form back to our legal team for sign-off. I've attached a draft amendment (Signed_Amendment_Draft.pdf) that incorporates our edits (not-yet-signed).

Two quick asks while we finalize language:
1) Can Laura confirm the export runbook timing (10 business days initiation + up to 90 calendar days completion)?
2) Ben / Marissa — can you confirm commercial treatment of the one-time pilot credit (30% on first-month invoice) and whether that impacts revenue recognition for our finance teams?

We'd like to lock this down this week; can we do a 30-min redline call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Best,
Sara
Sr. Procurement Manager
ClearPath Systems

Attachment: Signed_Amendment_Draft.pdf

Subject: Re: Questions on T&C: notice windows and auto-renew

Sara — great, glad we're converging. Confirmations: 

- Legal: Karthik will update clause to reflect "three (3) Pilot Orders" cap and 90-day export window.
- CS: Laura confirms runbook timing: initiate export within 10 business days, target completion within 90 calendar days; we'll include exceptions for very large datasets and will document any extra-cost migration tasks.
- Commercial: Ben confirms pilot credit treatment — 30% one-time credit applied to first post-activation invoice; finance has flagged internal memo but this is standard promotional treatment and won't delay signing.

We will update the order form and send the DocuSign link after Karthik's final language is inserted. Sara — please hold the 10am PT slot tomorrow; if anything changes we'll update. Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
